title: Material V1.5
description: What a surface is made of, as far as it acts on what reaches it: for sound, the fractions of energy it absorbs, scatters and lets through. Each fraction by frequency band; a renderer maps the bands given onto its own (for example 400 Hz, 2.5 kHz and 15 kHz).

Acoustic.description: How the surface acts on sound.

Absorption.description: Fraction of the sound energy reaching the surface that it absorbs.

Scattering.description: Fraction of the reflected energy scattered in random directions: 0 a mirror-like reflection, 1 a fully diffuse one.

Transmission.description: Fraction of the sound energy reaching the surface that passes through it.

BandScheme.description: The bands the per-band values are given in, by their centre frequencies: octave bands, one-third-octave bands, or others.

Incidence.description: How the values were measured or estimated: for sound arriving from all directions (random incidence, as in a reverberation room, ISO 354), or perpendicular to the surface (normal incidence, as in an impedance tube, ISO 10534). Values of different incidence are not directly comparable.
